stage_a.note: Bunim is highly energetic, smiling constantly, and delivers his pitch with pronounced, sustained positive engagement.
He shows sustained, pronounced excitement about his app, using animated gestures and a very upbeat tone.
He comes across as friendly and approachable, smiling warmly when introducing his friend Jesse.

venture.description: An online marketplace allowing users to rent private swimming pools by the hour.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim pitches Swimply, an app for renting private pools by the hour, demonstrating with a friend in a tub.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara jokes that she is not getting into the pool with the demonstrating friend.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if the business idea is actually real.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms that the business is real.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if the concept is essentially an Airbnb for swimming pools.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms Lori's comparison.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if the app is currently live on the app store.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms the app is live.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks for numbers on downloads, users, and revenue.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks how many pools are currently on the platform.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks who originally thought the business was a good idea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains he started it after offering to pay his neighbor to let his family use their empty pool.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin admits he initially thought the idea was crazy but likes it after hearing the origin story.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks what happened next in the company's development.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim details launching a beta site with his bar mitzvah money, getting initial pools, and raising early funding.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how much of his bar mitzvah money Bunim spent initially.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim states he spent ten thousand dollars of his own money and quickly booked nine hundred hours.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that Bunim is talking so fast he might spontaneously combust.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks Bunim to keep talking fast and asks about the nine hundred hours.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains they got their first hundred pools and raised nine hundred sixty thousand dollars to keep operating.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark clarifies in disbelief that Bunim raised nine hundred sixty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms the funding amount.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how much equity Bunim sold for that investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim replies he raised the money at a six million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks how Bunim managed to raise that much money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains a large pool maintenance company reached out to partner with them.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how many hours have been booked year to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim deflects the hours question, explaining he used the funds to develop a proper website.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if this is his third time trying to build the website.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim clarifies it is the first proper build after a beta version, taking three months to launch.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara tells Bunim to take a breath.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim returns to Mark's question, stating they booked sixteen hundred individual hours year to date.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks Bunim to walk through the financial model and how they make money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains hosts set prices, and Swimply takes a fifteen percent commission from hosts and ten from swimmers.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark confirms the total commission is twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms the total percentage.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much money the company has made year to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim states they did two hundred fifteen thousand in gross revenue, netting about twenty percent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark calculates and asks to confirm the net revenue is forty-two thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms the net revenue figure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert expresses amazement that Bunim raised a million dollars for the idea.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara challenges the high valuation, saying it makes no sense based on current revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim defends the valuation as a game of scale, promise, and future vision.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori says she sees the potential but doesn't want to invest, and is the first to exit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim accepts Lori's decision.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how customers handle bathroom needs when renting a pool.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains half of hosts offer a bathroom, while the other half choose the second option.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks what the second bathroom option is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim clarifies the second option is simply not offering a bathroom.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin suggests that without a bathroom, people will urinate in the pools.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim jokes that his demonstrating friend is currently peeing in the pool.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks for a sense of what customers are willing to pay for the rentals.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim states the average was forty-five dollars last year and ninety dollars this year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks if customers reuse the service regularly or if it is a one-time event.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim deflects the retention question, repeating the average hourly prices from the last two years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many people typically attend a booking that costs a hundred dollars an hour.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim answers that the average group size was seven last year and twelve this year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara states the idea is nuts and Bunim talks too fast, deciding to exit.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark challenges the market size, asking how many times a group of friends can afford to rent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains most users are families and details technical issues with their chat feature slowing approvals.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin exits, citing the crazy valuation compared to the low net revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim attempts to correct the revenue perception, stating they had a high volume of bookings with low completion.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin interrupts, reiterating that the valuation is still crazy regardless of the booking volume.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim counters with projections, claiming they will break even next year and profit fifteen million the following year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the fifteen million figure is gross revenue or overall profit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms it is profit and projects two hundred eighty-nine million in gross marketplace revenue by 2022.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark exits, criticizing Bunim's lack of self-awareness and stating his projections are completely disconnected from reality.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim defends himself, noting he is young, on his first business, and learning every day.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark acknowledges his hustle but insists that relying on unrealistic projections is a critical flaw.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim accepts the feedback, expressing a desire to work with the sharks to learn.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert exits, agreeing with Mark that projecting such massive growth so quickly is an impossible fantasy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim thanks the panel for their time.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin thanks Bunim as he leaves.

decisions.note: Exits because although she thinks he is onto something, she does not want to invest in it right now.
Exits because she thinks the idea is nuts, she doesn't get it, and the founder talks too fast.
Exits because the six million dollar valuation is crazy compared to making only twenty thousand dollars.
Exits because the founder lacks self-awareness and relies on unrealistic projections that are disconnected from reality.
Exits because the founder's projections of growing to two hundred eighty-nine million in three years are crazy and impossible.
